answer: A tight ring of 69 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Because the canyon calculation reruns each epoch, the ridge weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the ripple settlement publishes the resulting shares. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 27% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 25 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
